messages.author: 7e61879f0e11a028
messages.subject: Raster errors
parts:
I'm trying to save a 'Dsurface' object as a geotiff using 'raster'.  I can plot the Dsurface, summarize covariates, etc., but raster returns the following:

tmp <- raster(bbF1.predsurf2, values= covariates(bbF1.predsurf2)$bbM1.bbF1.D.0)

Warning message:
In matrix(tmp, nrow = ny, ncol = nx, byrow = TRUE) :
  data length [5476] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of columns [73]

Plot 'tmp' produces something that doesn't resemble my study area in the least.

These have worked in the past, and I can't identify what is different this time.  Thanks in advance for any pointers.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Raster errors
parts:
Hi Jeff
I think the S4 method defined in 'secr' for converting a mask to a raster has a second argument 'covariate' that is the name of the covariate with the values you want to use, so this should work
tmp <- raster(bbF1.predsurf2, 'bbM1.bbF1.D.0')
This seems to be undocumented and conflicts with examples in secr-noneuclidean.pdf - I'll have to fix that.

An example that works:
library(raster)
library(secr)
shorePossums <- predictDsurface(possum.model.Ds)
plot(raster(shorePossums, 'D.0'), useRaster = FALSE)
(useRaster = F seems necessary to make raster plot on my Windows machines).

Murray

parts:

I still can't put my finger on quite why your code didn't work, so my reply may not have helped. If you're still having trouble I'm guessing that the rectangularMask function of secr (used in raster())  failed because your mask was not aligned to the grid you used - maybe you imported a mask from somewhere else rather than constructing it in 'secr'? You could try
plot(rectangularMask(bbF1.predsurf2))

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Raster errors
parts:
We resolved this offline: there was a pesky bug in the S4 raster methods for mask and Dsurface objects: a matrix dimension computed as 73.999999 was truncated to 73 instead of rounded to 74.

I have documented these raster methods, added a 'crs' argument, compiled, checked etc. and uploaded the new working version of secr 2.9.5 to http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html. The code in secr-noneuclidean.pdf should still work, but I won't check that for a few weeks.

Murray

messages.author: e0fddb5311ed7959
messages.subject: Re: Raster errors
parts:
Hi Murray, 
Thanks for the response. 
tmask is the mask made from the traps object in my data. The warning appears regardless of whether i include the mask in the predictDsurface function or not, so I don't think it's that particular object but it sounds like it's definitely related to the trap layout. But for reference, here's what's creating the tmask object: 
> tmask = make.mask(traps(woylie.cap),spacing=50, buffer = 600, type = 'trapbuffer')

summary(tmask[[2]]) looks exactly how i would expect it to. 

After having a play around with the raster creation, including digging into the source code for the function, i think it's due to my trap layout (and as you say, therefore the mask) being non uniform across the study area and that is throwing off the step in the raster creation when the function tries to create a matrix from the extracted Dsurface data. 

Given that it seems to be my trap layout that's the problem, i have come up with the following workaround which gets me the raster i'm after (but it's probably not the most elegant solution). There may be better ways to go about this?

########################################
surf = Dsurf[[2]] # Get a Dsurface from particular session

# Extract relevant data from the Dsurface object
ras.data = data.frame(x=surf[,1],
                        y=surf[,2],
                        D.0 = covariates(surf)[,1])

ggplot(ras.data) + geom_tile(aes(x=x,y=y, fill=D.0)) # Check that the density data looks right when plotted

# Create the raster from the data
ras = raster::rasterFromXYZ(ras.data, res=spacing(surf), crs=sp::CRS("+init=epsg:32750"))
########################################

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Raster errors
parts:
On further investigation - Billy's usage exposed a limitation of rectangularMask() - it didn't work with a mask that had islands of habitat. I've rewritten it to allow for input masks with disjunct areas. A revised pre-release version is available at https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.3.2.zip (Windows binary) and https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.3.2.tar.gz (source). It would be good to test this some more before 4.3.2 goes to CRAN later this month. The problem should not arise when the mask is complete (type = 'traprect') (obviously you would not fit a model with such a large mask, but it could be used in predictDsurface).
Murray

We resolved this offline: there was a pesky bug in the S4 raster methods for mask and Dsurface objects: a matrix dimension computed as 73.999999 was truncated to 73 instead of rounded to 74.

I have documented these raster methods, added a 'crs' argument, compiled, checked etc. and uploaded the new working version of secr 2.9.5 to http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html. The code in secr-noneuclidean.pdf should still work, but I won't check that for a few weeks.
